answer: A countryside area I visited that I still think about fondly is a small farming village in Bogura district, about two hours from Sirajganj by road. I went there last year during the harvest season to visit a university friend's family, and although I know village life well from my grandparents' home, this place felt even more remote and peaceful. The village was surrounded by endless green paddy fields, and everything moved at a wonderfully [[leisurely]] pace. Most families there grow rice and vegetables, and many keep a few cows and chickens, so the day starts very early. What struck me most was how genuinely [[content]] the people seemed, despite having far fewer material comforts than people in towns and cities. My friend's mother cooked for us on a clay stove, and the food, fresh from their own fields and pond, was some of the best I have ever eaten. We spent our days walking along the narrow paths between the fields, and I even tried my hand at cutting rice, which was far harder than it looked. In the evenings we sat talking under a sky absolutely full of stars. The air was clean and the atmosphere was completely [[unhurried]]. Honestly, the experience gave me a real appreciation for a simpler way of life. It made me question how much of our constant rush is actually necessary. I came away feeling calm and strangely [[rejuvenated]], and I would love to spend more time somewhere like that, [[away from it all]].

followUps.q: Would you like to live in a village like that?
followUps.answer: For a few months, perhaps, but probably not permanently. I love the peace, but my work depends on good internet and being near clients, and I would miss the conveniences of town life.

Yes, quite rapidly. Most villages now have electricity, mobile phones and better roads, and many young people move away for work. Life is more comfortable, but some of the traditional community spirit is fading.

note: Located the village (Bogura, near Sirajganj) and acknowledged his own grandparents' village; 'city dwellers' and 'the city' adjusted to towns; added farming life and cooking; plain 'refreshed' mark replaced by 'rejuvenated', added 'away from it all'.
